title: Search for the reverse critical prime-phase inequality

verdict.conclusion: No independent proof of the reverse inequality was found. Hardy factorisation, Balazard--Saias--Yor and Nyman--Beurling/Burnol all isolate the same forbidden-zero Blaschke factor. Their desired vanishing, outerness, density or cyclicity statements are RH-equivalent, not established arithmetic upper bounds for the Stage-33 defect.

canonicalFactorisation.factorisation: f=B*O, where B is the Blaschke product of zeros with Re(rho)>1/2
canonicalFactorisation.stage33Relation: D_2 is a different positive kernel applied to the same off-line divisor; D_2=0 iff S_BSY=0 iff B=1 iff the Nyman distance is zero iff RH
canonicalFactorisation.logicalBarrier: canonical factorisation proves the plus sign and identifies the defect; it cannot prove B=1 from boundary or outer-factor data alone

candidateRoutes.establishedContent: For f(z)=C(1/(1-z)) the singular inner measure vanishes and f factors into its Blaschke zero factor and an outer factor.
candidateRoutes.whatItControls: the boundary data determine the outer factor; the right-half-plane zeros form the inner factor
candidateRoutes.circularityTest: declaring f outer, cyclic, or zero-inner is exactly the assertion that the Blaschke factor is one

candidateRoutes.establishedContent: (1/(2pi)) integral_(Re s=1/2) log|zeta(s)|/|s|^2 |ds| = sum_(Re rho>1/2) log|rho/(1-rho)| >= 0
candidateRoutes.whatItControls: a positive Green/Blaschke mass of every forbidden zero
candidateRoutes.reverseSignStatus: the inequality <=0 is equivalent to RH
candidateRoutes.circularityTest: assuming the integral vanishes assumes that the same inner zero divisor is absent

candidateRoutes.establishedContent: the Mellin image of the Nyman space is the Blaschke product times H^2, and the squared target distance is 1-|B(1)|^2
candidateRoutes.whatItControls: the complete off-line-zero inner factor, with no cancellation
candidateRoutes.reverseSignStatus: distance zero/cyclicity is equivalent to RH
candidateRoutes.circularityTest: density, cyclicity, or d_N tending to zero is the Nyman--Beurling criterion itself

candidateRoutes.establishedContent: integer dilations suffice in the Nyman--Beurling criterion
candidateRoutes.whatItControls: finite Gram distances converging to the Nyman closure distance
candidateRoutes.circularityTest: Gram positivity is automatic; convergence to zero imports Möbius cancellation at the critical scale

candidateRoutes.route: de Branges--Sonine completeness and spectral synthesis
candidateRoutes.establishedContent: unconditional complete/minimal zero systems and biorthogonal structures exist
candidateRoutes.whatItControls: representation and completeness of the actual zero system
candidateRoutes.circularityTest: the missing positive reflection metric or Hermite--Biehler property would encode RH

candidateRoutes.route: Nevanlinna negative squares or an integer index
candidateRoutes.establishedContent: an off-line zero can be represented by a quantised negative-index obstruction
candidateRoutes.whatItControls: detection without a collapsing metric amplitude
candidateRoutes.reverseSignStatus: no arithmetic computation proving index zero was found
candidateRoutes.circularityTest: computing the index from the analytic factor is only the argument-principle zero count

candidateRoutes.establishedContent: local explicit-formula and bounded commutator structures retain phase information
candidateRoutes.whatItControls: local completed terms, not a global zeta-sensitive vanishing index
candidateRoutes.reverseSignStatus: no global Fredholm or trace sign implying the reverse inequality was found
candidateRoutes.circularityTest: a proposed index must be computed arithmetically without first locating the zeros
candidateRoutes.classification: research proposal, not an established implication

candidateRoutes.route: critical Chebyshev energy or subexponential Laguerre growth
candidateRoutes.establishedContent: either condition would continue the relevant Mellin transform to Re s>1/2
candidateRoutes.whatItControls: zero-freeness of the whole right critical half-plane
candidateRoutes.circularityTest: both all-scale bounds are already RH-equivalent in the programme audit

verifiedTailBound.status: rigorous consequence of two established cited inputs
verifiedTailBound.bellottiWongBound: N(T)<=T/(2pi)log(T/(2pi e))+0.10076log T+0.24460loglog T+8.08344 for T>=e

exactCertificate.arithmetic: exact rational intervals; no floating-point proof comparisons

verifiedTailBound.doesNotImplyRh: a forbidden zero can be arbitrarily close to the critical line or sufficiently high, so the positive defect has no known uniform positive gap

collapsingMargin.highZeroAsymptotic: for fixed eta and large gamma, the BSY quartet mass is asymptotic to 2eta/gamma^2 and d_(eta,gamma) is asymptotic to 18eta^2/gamma^4, so d is asymptotic to (9/2) times the square of the BSY mass
collapsingMargin.consequence: finite verification and tail estimates can make D_2 extremely small but cannot round it to zero

secondaryDiagnosticOnly: GitHub route audits were used to locate literature and compare normalisations, not as proof authorities
the post-equivalence portfolio's negative-square and commutator proposals are research suggestions, not theorems implying RH
excludedSpeculativeClaims: an unvalidated GitHub catalogue entry claiming a 2026 zero-free half-plane Re(s)>7/8
self-published Balazard--Saias--Yor comparisons with inferred definitions or unsupported closure claims
evidenceAudit.excludedClaimReason: neither was verified as a correct primary proof; moreover a zero-free region Re(s)>7/8 would not exclude zeros in 1/2<Re(s)<=7/8 and therefore would not imply the target inequality

minimalOpenInput: supply genuinely arithmetic information proving that the right-half-plane Blaschke factor B is trivial; renaming this as outerness, cyclicity, zero Nyman distance, zero BSY mass, zero negative index, critical Chebyshev energy or defect-free phase continuation does not establish it
status: search closed with no reverse inequality; only equivalent inner-factor formulations and the rigorous near equality 0<=I_C^crit-C'/C(2)<9.274e-37 were obtained; RH remains open
